label: explode vs explode_outer
title: explode vs explode_outer: 3 rows or 5
definition: explode(col) turns an array column into rows: one row per element, and the other selected columns (order_id) repeat on every row. When the array is null or empty, explode returns no row, so that order disappears. explode_outer works the same way, but a null or empty array still gives one row, with a null element.
points: A05 data, 4 orders: 1001 items [A1, B2], 1002 [C3], 1003 [] (empty array), 1004 null.
explode("items") returns 3 rows: 1001 twice, 1002 once. Orders 1003 and 1004 are gone.
explode_outer("items") returns 5 rows: the same 3, plus 1003 and 1004 with a null item.
posexplode adds pos and col (pos starts at 0) and also skips null or empty arrays. posexplode_outer keeps them.
Need every order, even ones with no items? Use explode_outer. Exam guide Section 3, Data Transformation and Modeling (exploding arrays).
example_note: A05 example, fictional orders read from a Unity Catalog volume in Databricks Free Edition (serverless notebook).
code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import explode, explode_outer
orders.select("order_id", explode("items").alias("item")).count()        # 3
orders.select("order_id", explode_outer("items").alias("item")).count()  # 5
misconception: explode does not return a null row for an empty or null array. It drops the row. Only the _outer variants keep it.
memory_trick: OUTER keeps the outsiders. The empty array and the null stay in.
remember: explode: 3 rows. explode_outer: 5 rows. If you need orders with no items, use explode_outer.
